missionPremise: Operator ruling in the SS-W17 dispatch: tier2 flood is retired for being wrong, and NO consumer is repointed to the flood-hazard-fact atom until that atom carries a containment check. SS-W11 scored the atom 5,714 of 5,714 against FEMA NFHL; that is evidence, not a guarantee, and tier2 would also have passed an adjudication of one parcel that happened to sit near a tile centre. Without the check the retirement swaps one unchecked hazard determination for another that currently happens to be right, and buys a better number rather than a better instrument. Sources: P:/doc_repo/_dispatches/2026-08-19_ss-w17_dispatch.md, P:/doc_repo/_inbox/2026-08-19_ss-w11_close.json, P:/tmp/data fix/61_enforcement_doctrine.md, P:/tmp/data fix/enforcement.mdc.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (a) point at the code that refuses a flood determination whose query point is not inside the parcel it answers for, (b) run one command that observes that refusal firing on real production parcels, (c) name the executor, trigger, failure mode and BYPASSES of the standing check without being told, and (d) see that item 1.0 did not run and why. MET for (a) through (d). NOT MET, and deliberately so, for the thing a reader might assume follows: no stored atom carries a containment stamp, so the corpus is still unchecked and no consumer was repointed.
scopeBasis: The dispatch scopes this lane to repo hauska-engine and one worktree, and gates item 1.0 on 0.7 passing. Deliberately EXCLUDED and named so the omission reads as deliberate: (1) the hauska-map and legacy-design-tools repoints and the tier2 writer retirement, which are other repos with no worktree, no branch and no PR provided by this dispatch — the ORPHAN is named explicitly below per the paired-retirement rule; (2) the flood corpus re-bake, which takes the atoms writer slot and is an operator-sequenced apply while this lane is read-only; (3) any deploy, per the hard rules; (4) the contract change that would make the sampling stamp a first-class atom-contract field, which lives in hauska-atom-contract.

gateVerdict.verdict: 0.7 IS BUILT AND PROVEN IN CODE. 0.7 IS NOT SATISFIED IN DATA. ITEM 1.0 THEREFORE DID NOT RUN.
gateVerdict.reasoning: The dispatch gates 1.0 on the containment check existing and the promoted harness having run against the replacement. Both happened. But the harness's verdict on the replacement is FAIL: 5,750 of 5,750 sampled Bastrop atoms carry no sample point and no containment state, because every stored flood atom predates the gate. Repointing consumers now would point them at determinations that have never been containment-checked, which is precisely what the operator ruled against. The CODE carries the check; the DATA does not. The gate opens after a re-bake under the gate, which this lane cannot run.

deliverable_0_7a_containmentCheck.whatItChecks: The FEMA query point must fall inside the parcel ring it answers for. Ray cast against the outer ring, holes respected, EVERY MultiPolygon part tested rather than only the first.
deliverable_0_7a_containmentCheck.whyItIsMeaningShaped: Two inputs that must agree, and the predicate that joins them is a different computation from the one that produced the point. No sentinel satisfies both: a tile centre, a bounding-box centre, a (0,0), a NaN, or a point copied from a neighbouring parcel all fail containment, and a fabricated ring yields no verdict rather than a passing one.
deliverable_0_7a_containmentCheck.threeStatesNeverCollapsed: contained, not-contained, unmeasurable. The policy over them is a SEPARATE pure function (floodDeterminationGate), so a policy change cannot quietly redefine a state.
deliverable_0_7a_containmentCheck.policy: not-contained REFUSES. unmeasurable REFUSES when the derivation is bbox-centre, declared or none, because then neither derivation ties the point to the parcel. unmeasurable EMITS and is marked when the source publishes a Point geometry, because that point IS the parcel's own published location.
enforcedByTypeNotOnlyByCheck: PlannedPresentFloodHazard and PlannedAbsentFloodHazard are stamped EmittableContainmentState = Exclude<ContainmentState,'not-contained'>. A determination made outside its parcel cannot be CONSTRUCTED as a published record, at any consumer, with no trigger to be missing and no call site to be skipped. TypeScript proved the runtime guard unreachable, which is how we know the type is load-bearing: tsc raised TS2367 on the guard.
Refusals live in plan.refused, a DIFFERENT ARRAY from the one buildAtomsForFloodHazardPlan iterates, so a refusal cannot become an atom by omission or by a future edit.
FloodDeterminationGateResult is a DISCRIMINATED UNION on decision, so { decision:'emit', reasonCode:'sample-point-outside-parcel' } is a compile error rather than a review responsibility.
FloodParcelInput.geometry is REQUIRED, so 'this caller never thought about the ring' is a compile error rather than a silent third state.
otherFailClosedEdges: Both plan backends skip refused parcels before querying, so the value is never computed rather than computed and discarded.
verifyStoredFloodHazardFactAtom now reads the STORED BYTES and fails on a missing stamp or a not-contained stamp; the writer throws on the first verify failure in a batch.
digestFloodPlan covers the refusal set, so a plan that stops refusing gets a different hash and cannot replay under a matching digest.
drainFloodPlanPayload FAILS CLOSED on any --from-plan artifact written before the gate existed.

independentlyDerivedClassification.question: Under the narrowed rule, is the containment check meaning-shaped or is it internal consistency?
independentlyDerivedClassification.myClassification: MEANING-SHAPED, but by a narrower and weaker claim than the phrase usually carries, and the strict two-party test is right to be suspicious.
independentlyDerivedClassification.reasoning: The two sides are not two fields from one upstream. The RING is TxGIO's assertion about the parcel; the POINT is OUR arithmetic mean of that ring's vertices. One party did not produce both: the source produced one and our transformation produced the other, and TxGIO acting alone cannot make our vertex mean land outside its own concave ring, because that is a property of our algorithm. So the check catches OUR TRANSFORMATION ERROR, and it caught it: 229 real parcels.
independentlyDerivedClassification.whatItCannotCatch: It cannot catch SOURCE error. If TxGIO published the wrong ring for a parcel, our centroid would sit happily inside that wrong ring and the check would pass. Every verdict here is conditional on the ring being the right parcel's ring, and nothing in this lane tests that.
independentlyDerivedClassification.whereTheStrictTestBites: The bbox-centre branch. There, both the bbox columns and the geometry column come from the same ingest of the same source, so containment against a bbox-derived point WOULD be one derivation wearing two hats. That branch is exactly the branch the gate REFUSES rather than passing, which is a consistency worth noting: the case where the two-party test fails is the case where the check declines to answer.
independentlyDerivedClassification.feedbackOnTheRule: The rule as narrowed would classify this check as internal consistency if 'same upstream record' is the test, and that would be the wrong call, because the error class it catches is real, is ours, and is invisible to every presence-shaped check. I would widen the rule to name SOURCE-VERSUS-OUR-DERIVATION as a third admissible shape, with the explicit caveat that it catches our error and not theirs, so it is never quoted as evidence the source is right. A genuinely two-party version of this check exists and is not built: compare the ring's area against the CAD roll's recorded acreage for the same parcel, which are two parties describing one thing.
independentlyDerivedClassification.aSecondImplementationIsNotASecondDERIVAT: The PostGIS ST_Contains leg is a second IMPLEMENTATION of one predicate, not a second derivation of one fact. It catches our coding error, not our sampling error. It is reported as a divergence test and never as independent corroboration.

freeFindings.text: `main` is NOT branch-protected on empressaioemail-tech/hauska-engine. VERIFIED: the protection endpoint returns 404 'Branch not protected'. Every CI check in this repository, including the ones this lane added and the ones that predate it, is a red X rather than a block. Any close in this program that has described a CI check as a 'blocked merge' has overstated it. This is a repository-settings action for the operator, not a code change.

229 of 5,750 sampled Bastrop parcels (3.98 percent) carry a flood determination made at a point outside the parcel, a median 15.3 m out and up to 164 m out. Extrapolated naively to Bastrop's 62,256 flood atoms that is roughly 2,480 parcels, but that extrapolation is NOT measured and the first 6,000 features by feature_index are not a random sample. The measured claim is 229 of 5,750.

The tier2 retirement's own consumer set includes a hazard the dispatch did not name: packages/retrieval/src/serving-sweep/project-sheet.ts encodes THREE distinct served-flood states whose reason strings are all tier2-named. Deleting them with the tier2 plumbing removes the only mechanism that can distinguish a correctly repointed reader from a silently broken one. Repoint before retire applies inside this file, not only across repos.

The dispatch's 'nine engine instruments' is not reproducible at d3f3794: twenty tracked files match, and the detector and the harness it asks to bucket separately are two subcommands of ONE script. A file-level three-bucket move cannot be executed as described.

138 of the first 6,000 Bastrop parcel features carry an unusable prop_id (blank or all-zero) and are silently skipped by the writer, so they have no flood atom and no record anywhere that they were skipped. skippedUnusableKey is counted in the plan summary but never persisted. A parcel that exists in txgio_parcel and has no atom is indistinguishable, from the store, from one that was never processed.

geometryCentroid takes the FIRST part of a MultiPolygon only, so a multi-part parcel's determination is made about whichever part happens to be first in the coordinate array. The containment check makes this SAFE (the point is verified inside that part) but does not make it REPRESENTATIVE: a two-part parcel gets an answer about one part with nothing recording which. The stamp now records the point, so this is at least recoverable after the fact.

The bbox-centre fallback fired ZERO times in Bastrop because every parcel has a ring, so the branch most similar to the tier2 defect is entirely unexercised by the only county measured. Its behaviour under the new gate (refuse) is proven only by unit test, never against production data.

constraintsHonored: READ-ONLY against both production databases: SELECT only. No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or DDL was issued against hauska_mcp or neondb. No atoms writer slot taken. No re-bake run.
